Steve Sarkisian: 'Everything' To Be Evaluated, Including Arch Manning
results.description: Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said everything will be evaluated, including quarterback Arch Manning, after Saturday's 27-24 home loss to Florida. It was the Longhorns' second straight loss. "Everything's going to be evaluated," said Sarkisian. When asked whether that included a quarterback change, Sarkisian answered directly. "Everything means everything," said Sarkisian. Florida linebacker Myles Graham forced a fumble on a sack of Manning with just under two minutes left, and the Gators ran out the clock. A week earlier, Texas lost a 17-7 lead to Oklahoma on a walk-off field goal after two fourth-quarter interceptions by Manning. Manning completed 14 of 20 passes for 173 yards and a touchdown. He was sacked five times. He led a late drive that included a 62-yard completion to Emmett Mosley and a touchdown pass to Cam Coleman to make it 27-24. "Was Arch perfect? No," said Sarkisian. "But nobody was perfect on offense today." Manning said he has not lost confidence and accepts the scrutiny. "Everyone's evaluated every week…" said Manning. "Everyone's got to get better, and it starts with me." Texas led 17-3 in the first half but scored only seven points the rest of the game. The Longhorns went 2-for-10 on third down and 1-for-3 on fourth down. Star edge rusher Colin Simmons left in the fourth quarter on a cart with an apparent right leg injury. He came into the game leading the nation with 9.5 sacks. Florida backup Tramell Jones Jr. threw two touchdown passes in his first college start. Jadan Baugh ran for 88 yards and a touchdown. Texas is now 4-2 and has a 56% chance to make the College Football Playoff, according to The Athletic's projections.
